lead: Puerperal pyrexia = temperature ≥ 38 °C in the first 14 days after birth. Puerperal sepsis = genital tract infection from ROM or labour to day 42. Sepsis is the leading cause of maternal death in Sudan; infection is usually polymicrobial and ascends to the placental site.
f: Definition

Puerperal morbidity: ≥ 38 °C on any 2 of the first 10 days, not counting the first 24 h · Puerperal sepsis (WHO): ≥ 2 of pelvic pain, fever ≥ 38.5 °C, abnormal discharge, foul smell, slow involution · Maternal sepsis (WHO): organ dysfunction from infection in pregnancy, birth, after abortion or to day 42
Causes and day of onset

Endometritis is the commonest cause · Order by day: chest (day 1 after GA) → urine and womb (day 2–5) → wound (day 5–7) → breast and legs · Also retained products, infected haematoma, cannula site, epidural abscess, drug fever, malaria or typhoid in endemic areas
Organisms

Group A strep: most lethal; from a sore throat via hands; looks well, then sudden toxic shock · Anaerobes (Bacteroides): commonest in endometritis · E. coli, Klebsiella: UTI, endotoxic shock · Staph. aureus: mastitis, wound · Clostridium: after unsafe abortion
Risk factors
Caesarean section (5–20 times the risk) · Long labour, ROM > 24 h, many VEs · Retained placenta, manual removal, PPH · Anaemia, diabetes, obesity, HIV · Sore throat in the family (GAS)
Clinical features

Fever ≥ 38 °C or < 36 °C, rigors, tachycardia · Severe: low BP, confusion, mottled skin, little urine, pain out of proportion (GAS, necrotising infection) · Endometritis: foul lochia, tender bulky uterus · Breast: red wedge · Urinary: loin pain, rigors · DVT: tender swollen calf

sc: Day 2, severe pain needing morphine, child with a sore throat → Group A strep sepsis: antibiotics now
Loin pain, rigors, catheter in labour → Pyelonephritis

f: Recognising sepsis early

MEOWS chart: 1 red or 2 yellow triggers → urgent review · Red: temperature < 35 or ≥ 38 °C, systolic < 90, pulse > 120, RR > 30, SpO₂ < 95% · Obstetric qSOFA ≥ 2: RR ≥ 25, systolic < 90, altered mental state · Septic shock: low BP despite fluids or lactate ≥ 4 → ICU

tr: A normal temperature does not exclude sepsis: hypothermia and tachycardia are worse signs

f: Investigations

Blood cultures before antibiotics · high vaginal swab, MSU, wound and throat swabs · FBC, lactate, CRP, U&E, LFT, clotting · Malaria film or RDT in every fever · Pelvic ultrasound: retained products, collection · CT if fever persists
Differential diagnosis
Malaria · typhoid · pyelonephritis · appendicitis · PE · transfusion reaction · drug fever · meningitis after spinal

tr: Never wait for culture results or a "second fever" to treat a sick woman

f: Sepsis Six: the first hour

Give: oxygen, IV fluids, IV antibiotics · Take: blood cultures, lactate, urine output · Each hour of delay raises the risk of death · Call help, MEOWS every 15–30 min; septic shock → ICU, vasopressors
Antibiotics

Endometritis, sepsis: clindamycin 900 mg IV 8-hourly + gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV daily (WHO) · Alternatives: ceftriaxone + metronidazole; ampicillin + gentamicin + metronidazole (local units often start ceftriaxone + metronidazole) · Severe sepsis: piperacillin-tazobactam or meropenem + clindamycin (stops GAS toxin) · Mastitis: flucloxacillin; keep feeding · Pyelonephritis: ceftriaxone IV · IV until 48 h fever-free; no oral course after uncomplicated endometritis · Avoid tetracyclines and chloramphenicol

sc: Fever, foul lochia, tender uterus after CS → Clindamycin + gentamicin

f: Supportive and surgical care

Fluids, oxygen, enoxaparin 40 mg daily · Evacuate retained products after antibiotics start · Drain pus (breast, wound, pelvic abscess) · Debride necrotising fasciitis early · Hysterectomy if the uterus is necrotic

sc: Still febrile after 3 days of antibiotics, bulky uterus → Ultrasound for retained products; evacuate

f: Complications

Septic shock, MODS · DIC · Pelvic abscess: swinging fever, diarrhoea, tenesmus → drain · Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis: ovarian vein after CS, spiking fever on antibiotics, looks well → add heparin · Necrotising fasciitis · Secondary PPH · Late: tubal block, infertility

tr: Fever on antibiotics is rarely "resistant bacteria": look for pus, retained products, pelvic vein thrombosis, DVT, malaria

f: Prevention

Treat anaemia and bacteriuria · Hand washing before every examination, few VEs, partograph · CS prophylaxis before skin incision: cefuroxime 1.5 g or cefazolin 2 g IV (allergy: clindamycin); avoid co-amoxiclav before birth (NEC) · Check the placenta is complete · Peripheral unit: first IV dose before referral
